<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="100.7.116.115" /></noinclude><section begin="par108" />supported by the rather numerous examples of cohortative forms after {{GHGterm|wāw consec.}} of the imperfect (cf. {{GHGpar|49|e}}, as also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=66|verse=6}} {{GHGheb|text=שָׁם נִשְׂמְחָה|translate=there did we rejoice}}<ref>Analogous to this cohortative (as equivalent to the imperfect) after {{GHGheb|text=שָׁם}} is the use of the historic imperf. after {{GHGheb|text=אָז}}, {{GHGpar|107|c}}.</ref>; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=119|verse=163}} {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֲתַעֵ֑בָה}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=7|verse=7}}), which can likewise only be explained as forms chosen merely for euphony, and therefore due to considerations of rhythm.

{{GHGmargin-letter|108|h}}
2. The cohortative is strange after {{GHGheb|text=עַד־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=73|verse=17}} ''until I went''... {{GHGheb|text=אָבִ֫ינָה|translate=I considered their latter end}}; possibly a pregnant construction for ‘until I made up my mind, saying, I will consider’, &c. (but {{GHGheb|text=אָבִ֫ינָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=7|verse=7}} is still dependent on the preceding {{GHGheb|text=וָ}}); {{GHGheb|text=עַד־אַרְגִּ֫יעָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=12|verse=19}} is at any rate to be explained in the same way (in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=49|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=50|verse=44|hidebook=1}} we have {{GHGheb|text=כִּי־א׳}} with a similar meaning), ''as long as I'' (intentionally) ''wink with the eyelashes'' (shall wink). On the other hand, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=32|verse=30}} {{GHGheb|text=אֲכַפֵּר}} is to be read, with the Samaritan, instead of {{GHGheb|text=אֲכַפְּרָה}} after {{GHGheb|text=אוּלַי}}.
<section end="par108" />
<section begin="par109" />{{GHGpar-heading|109|Use of the Jussive}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|109|a}}
As the ''cohortative'' is used in the 1st pers., so the {{GHGterm|jussive}} is especially found in the 2nd and 3rd pers. sing. and plur. to express a more or less definite desire that something should or should not happen (cf. for its form, which frequently coincides with that of the ordinary {{GHGterm|imperfect}},<ref>With regard to verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, it is true that the full form of the imperfect is frequently used with the meaning of the jussive (as also for the cohortative, see {{GHGpar|108|a}}, note 2), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אַל־יִרְאֶה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=3|verse=9}} (but previously {{GHGheb|text=יְקַו|translate=let it look for!}}): especially ''in'' ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=2|verse=3}}) and immediately ''before'' the principal pause, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=תֵּֽרָאֶה}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=39}} {{GHGheb|text=יִהְֽיֶה}}, but previously {{GHGheb|text=יְהִי־נָא}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=47|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=תֵּֽרָאֶה}}, previously {{GHGheb|text=תִּגָּל}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=109|verse=7}}. On the attempt to distinguish such jussives from the imperfect by means of a special meaning {{GHGheb|text=־ֵה}}, see {{GHGpar|75|hh}}.</ref> {{GHGpar|48|f}}, ''g''). More particularly its uses may be distinguished as follows:

1. The {{GHGterm|jussive}} standing alone, or co-ordinated with another jussive:

{{GHGmargin-letter|109|b}}
(''a'') In affirmative sentences to express a command, a wish (or a blessing), advice, or a request; in the last case (the optative or precative) it is frequently strengthened by the addition of {{GHGheb|text=נָא}}. Examples: {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=יְהִי אוֹר|translate=let there be light!}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=6}}, 9, 11, &c. (the creative commands); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=6|verse=26}} ''the Lord lift up his countenance upon thee, and give thee peace!'' cf. verse 25. After particles expressing a wish, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=34}} {{GHGheb|text=לוּ יְהִי}} ''I would it might be;'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=81|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=אִם־תִּשְׁמַע־לִי|translate=if thou wouldest hearken unto me!}} As a humble request, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=44|verse=33}}... {{GHGheb|text=יֵֽשֶׁב־נָא עַבְדְּךָ... וְהַנַּ֫עַר יַ֫עַל|translate=let thy servant, I pray thee, abide}}, &c., ''and let the lad go up, &c.'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=47|verse=4}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|109|c}}
(''b'') In negative sentences to express prohibition or dissuasion, warning, a negative wish (or imprecation), and a request. The prohibitive particle used before the jussive (according to {{GHGpar|107|o}}) is almost always {{GHGheb|text=אַל־}} (in negative desires and requests frequently<section end="par109" /><noinclude>
